direction: Diverse population with rotation-aligned crossover, not single-incumbent hopping. Generate a pool of 6–10 genuinely distinct local optima by running short softmax+LP optimisations from independent random starts and from large ($ \sigma\ge0.15$) perturbations of the record, keeping a candidate only if its contact graph (pairs within $10^{-6}$ of its max) differs from every pooled graph by a substantial Hamming distance and its max cosine is below $\sim0.86$; this preserves multiple basins instead of collapsing to one. For crossover, align a pair of parents with `scipy.linalg.orthogonal_procrustes`, cut the sphere by a random hyperplane through the origin (in a random direction in $\mathbb{R}^4$), take the points of parent A on one side and parent B on the other, resolve duplicates/overlaps by greedy matching and refill any shortfall from the largest voids, then anneal and LP-polish the child. Additionally generate some parents by optimising overloaded codes of 156–160 points and deleting the highest-contact-load points back to 153, since squeeze-out from a denser problem lands in different topologies. Iterate selection–crossover–polish, always retaining the best few *distinct* graphs in the pool, and return the best final LP-polished child.

idea: Break the jammed 152-plus-rattler core by opening new balanced basins with 17x9 parallel Hopf-fiber initializations plus localized cap/cage surgery around the rattler hole and overloaded points, each driven by annealed softmax Riemannian-Adam and trust-region LP polishing.
Symmetric 9x17 torus-orbit ansatz with twist multipliers optimized by annealed softmax Adam to get a balanced rattler-free basin, then released-symmetry softmax descent and trust-region LP polishing.
direction: Symmetric torus/orbit ansatz with no rattlers by construction. Build the code from 9 orbits of size 17 under simultaneous rotation by $2\pi/17$ in two orthogonal 2-planes: orbit $j$ has points $\bigl(r_j\cos(\theta_j+2\pi k/17),\, r_j\sin(\theta_j+2\pi k/17),\, \sqrt{1-r_j^2}\cos(\phi_j+2\pi m_j k/17),\, \sqrt{1-r_j^2}\sin(\phi_j+2\pi m_j k/17)\bigr)$ for $k=0,\dots,16$, with per-orbit parameters $r_j,\theta_j,\phi_j$ and a small set of twist multipliers $m_j$ coprime to 17, giving $9\times17=153$ points and only $\sim$30 free parameters. Every point in an orbit has identical contact counts, so a rattler is impossible and load is balanced automatically. Optimise the parameters with annealed softmax Adam over the full expanded Gram matrix, trying several $(m_j)$ patterns and random parameter restarts; then release the symmetry—use the best symmetric code as a seed for unrestricted softmax descent and LP polishing so the final code may break symmetry slightly while retaining the balanced topology. Also try nearby orbit decompositions (e.g. mixed orbit sizes from signed-permutation orbits plus a few free points) if the 9$\times$17 family plateaus.

idea: Target-cosine feasibility with quartic violation energy and continuation warm-starts plus violating-pair kicks and short LP polishes.
direction: Sub-record target-cosine feasibility attack instead of minimising the max. Fix target values $t\in\{0.8488, 0.8485, 0.8480, 0.8475\}$ strictly below the record and minimise the differentiable violation energy $E_t=\sum_{i<j}\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)^4$ (or a softplus analogue) by Riemannian Adam/L-BFGS on the sphere, starting both from perturbed copies of `best.npy` and from fresh random codes. Any configuration with $E_t=0$ is automatically a new record, and this formulation can pass through configurations whose current max is worse than the record—exactly the barrier crossing that greedy min-max polishing forbids. Use continuation: solve for $t=0.850$, then decrease $t$ in steps of $2\times10^{-4}$, warm-starting each stage; interleave short LP polishes, and if a stage stalls with a small set of violating pairs, apply targeted kicks only to the endpoints of violating pairs and resume. Spend the budget sweeping the lowest targets rather than re-polishing the known optimum.

idea: Break the jammed 152+1 isostatic core by hole-targeted collective moves (rattler-neighbor expansion, hub relocation to largest empty caps, cap deletion) with annealed soft-max repulsion and Metropolis wandering plus final trust-region LP squeeze.
Dual-stress-guided contact surgery that forces second-shell pairs up while releasing zero-stress contacts via penalized soft-max annealing plus LP re-polish over new topologies.
direction: Dual-stress-guided contact surgery. Run the LP polish once and extract the dual variables (HiGHS inequality marginals) on the $\sim$460 active contacts; contacts with near-zero stress are candidates for release, while second-shell pairs (rank $\sim$460--1000, slack $10^{-5}$--$2\times10^{-3}$), especially those incident to the rattler or to points with $\le$4 contacts, are candidates for forced new contacts. For each of $\sim$30 trials, choose 1--3 forced pairs and 3--8 released contacts, then solve a penalized problem: minimize soft-max$_{\beta}$ of all cosines with $\beta$ annealed $50\to400$, plus a penalty $\lambda\sum_{\rm forced}\mathrm{relu}(t_{\rm target}-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)$ that pulls the chosen pairs up to $t_{\rm target}=$ record $-2\times10^{-4}$ while the released contacts are allowed to drop, followed by LP polish. Accept a trial into the incumbent pool if its contact graph differs from the record graph by at least 5 edges and its score is within $5\times10^{-4}$, then re-polish from it with a fresh LP; this directly searches neighbouring graph topologies that random kicking almost never reaches because it requires several contacts to break simultaneously.

idea: Rattler-centred patch deletion with void refill and target-driven anneal to change contact topology, then LP squeeze.
direction: Rattler-centred patch deletion and refill. Identify the rattler (contact count 0 at tolerance $10^{-7}$) and, in successive trials, delete it together with the 7, 11, or 15 points having largest cosine to it (or to a randomly chosen hub point), freeze the remaining $\sim$140 points, and reinsert the deleted points one at a time at the largest spherical voids of the current set (maximize the minimum angle over $20{,}000$ random candidates plus local refinement). Then optimize only the reinserted points with an annealed soft-max objective at target cosine $0.849102- \delta$ for $\delta\in\{10^{-4},3\times10^{-4},10^{-3}\}$ (penalize $\mathrm{relu}(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle - t_{\rm target})$ over pairs involving a moved point), unfreeze all points for a short soft-max anneal, and finish with the existing trust-region LP. Cycle over patch centres (rattler first, then random points and highest-contact hubs), keeping any candidate whose post-LP score is within $0.002$ of the incumbent for one extra all-free anneal, since the useful event is a changed contact graph, not immediate improvement.

Adiabatic 152-insertion plus 154-deletion homotopy to redistribute the rattler slack into a new contact topology.
direction: Particle-number homotopy through $N=152$ and $N=154$. First delete the rattler and LP-polish the resulting 152-point code, which should drop well below $0.8491$ and has a genuinely different, less frustrated contact structure; record its largest voids over a dense random sample. Reinsert a 153rd point at the best void but introduce it adiabatically: give the new point a repulsion weight $\lambda$ ramped $0\to1$ in $\sim$10 stages, at each stage running soft-max Adam ($\beta:30\to250$, learning rate $0.005\to0.0005$) plus a 1--2 s LP polish, so the core opens a cavity gradually rather than being kicked. Run the symmetric variant too: duplicate the rattler with a small offset to make 154 points, optimize briefly, delete the point whose removal gives the lowest polished 153-point score over $\sim$20 candidate deletions, and polish. Allocate roughly half the time budget to several insertion voids from the 152-code and half to deletion choices from the 154-code, always retaining the unmodified record as a fallback return value.

idea: Symmetric orbit seeds with few-parameter search then symmetry release and annealing plus LP polish, keeping the most dissimilar near-record basin for final jam.
direction: Structured symmetric seeds unrelated to the record. Generate starting codes from low-parameter orbit families on $S^3$: (a) Clifford-torus layers, points $(\cos a_k\cos\theta,\cos a_k\sin\theta,\sin a_k\cos\phi,\sin a_k\sin\phi)$ over grids in $\theta,\phi$ with a few layer latitudes $a_k$ and phase offsets, with layer sizes summing to 153 (e.g. $17\times9$); (b) quaternion-group orbits, acting by left multiplication by the 24 binary-tetrahedral or 120 binary-icosahedral unit quaternions on 1--7 generic seed quaternions (orbit sizes 24 or 120, combined and trimmed/padded to 153); (c) subsets of the 600-cell (120 vertices) plus a rotated 24-cell and a small generic orbit. Optimize each family first in its few symmetric parameters (Nelder--Mead or random search on latitudes, phases, and relative rotations, scored by exact max cosine), take the best 3--4 families, then release the symmetry and run soft-max annealing followed by LP polish. These seeds have regular contact graphs and balanced contact counts by construction; even a symmetric seed scoring $\sim$0.86 is valuable if, after release and LP, its contact graph differs substantially from the record graph, so log graph edit distance alongside score and spend the final 30 s polishing the most dissimilar candidate that is within $0.003$ of the incumbent.

idea: Cooperative patch-shift plus contact-rewiring basin-hopping with Metropolis acceptance on LP-polished values to force a different contact graph and eliminate the rattler.
Rattler-centred patch deletion with void refill, targeted softplus annealing and LP polishing.
direction: Rattler-centred patch deletion and refill. Identify the rattler (contact count 0 at tolerance $10^{-7}$) and, in successive trials, delete it together with the 7, 11, or 15 points having largest cosine to it (or to a randomly chosen hub point), freeze the remaining $\sim$140 points, and reinsert the deleted points one at a time at the largest spherical voids of the current set (maximize the minimum angle over $20{,}000$ random candidates plus local refinement). Then optimize only the reinserted points with an annealed soft-max objective at target cosine $0.849102- \delta$ for $\delta\in\{10^{-4},3\times10^{-4},10^{-3}\}$ (penalize $\mathrm{relu}(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle - t_{\rm target})$ over pairs involving a moved point), unfreeze all points for a short soft-max anneal, and finish with the existing trust-region LP. Cycle over patch centres (rattler first, then random points and highest-contact hubs), keeping any candidate whose post-LP score is within $0.002$ of the incumbent for one extra all-free anneal, since the useful event is a changed contact graph, not immediate improvement.

idea: Cooperative basin-hopping with patch rotations, largest-hole refill and Riesz-to-softmax annealing plus trust-region LP to change the contact topology.

Escape the rigid record basin with cooperative multi-point moves (cap deletion with sequential hole reinsertion, hemisphere twist, greedy farthest-point splice of two parents, and rattler-neighbourhood shakes) followed by momentum hinge annealing and trust-region LP polishing.

Continue in N away from the over-jammed 153-point optimum by deleting to N=148 and re-adding through voids and by growing to N=160 then greedily deleting, fully re-optimising with soft-max annealing plus trust-region LP at every N to force a new contact topology.
direction: Use continuation in $N$ to enter from a different basin: first fully optimise codes for $N=148,\dots,152$ (starting from the record with the rattler and highest per-point-max points removed, soft-max anneal plus LP at each $N$), then greedily add the 153rd point at the largest spherical void found by dense random sampling and re-optimise all points. In the reverse direction, optimise $N=156$--$160$ codes seeded from the record plus void insertions, then delete points one at a time, always removing the point whose removal most reduces the remaining maximum (recomputing after short re-optimisations), until $N=153$ is reached, and LP-polish; both paths change the contact topology by construction rather than by perturbation size.

idea: Rattler-centred defect surgery with frozen greedy refill and two-stage soft-max Adam plus LP squeeze.
direction: Perform rattler-centred defect surgery: identify the rattler and, in successive trials, delete it together with $k=4,6,8,12$ points chosen from its nearest neighbours and from 7-8-contact hubs, freeze the remaining points, and refill the deleted points one at a time by sampling 100k-200k random unit vectors and inserting each at the vector minimising its maximum cosine to the currently kept/frozen set (with small random jitter). Then optimise only the refilled points and their neighbours within cosine $>0.75$ for 500-1000 soft-max Adam steps (beta $50\to300$), unfreeze all points for another 1000 steps, and finish with the trust-region LP; cycle over $k$ and random seeds within the time budget and keep a candidate even if its pre-LP score is up to 0.005 worse than the incumbent, since the point is to change which points pin the rattler.

idea: Break hub-incident contact edges with hinge-penalized soft-max rewiring then exclusion-aware LP polishing with taboo and 0.002-accept wandering.
direction: Force contact-graph rewiring instead of point kicks: from the incumbent contact graph (slack $<10^{-9}$), randomly select 15-40 contact edges, biased toward edges incident to hubs, and run soft-max optimisation with those selected pairs given an extra repulsion or an explicit target cosine $\le \text{current max}-\delta$ for $\delta\in\{3\cdot10^{-4},10^{-3},3\cdot10^{-3}\}$, while all other pairs keep the usual soft-max weight, so the selected edges are deliberately broken at a temporarily worse score. Follow with LP polishing in which the broken edges are initially excluded from the active set (added back only if they rise above max$-10^{-6}$), accept the polished result as the new current configuration if it is within 0.002 of the best (not only if it improves), and repeat, tracking the edge set so successive iterations do not simply re-form the same graph.

idea: Continue in N both ways — collapse to N=148 by deleting the rattler plus worst points then regrow to 153 by void insertion, and expand to N=158 by void insertion then greedily delete the point minimizing the remaining max, with soft-max annealing plus trust-region LP at every N.

idea: Large-neighborhood cap reinsertion with degree-balanced local annealing to rewire the over-jammed contact graph and free the rattler.

idea: Hub-to-void transplantation plus coherent cap rotations with annealed soft-max repulsion and LP polishing to replace the over-jammed hub/rattler graph by a balanced rattler-free isostatic graph.
Break hub-incident contacts deliberately with boosted soft-max repulsion then LP-polish with those edges excluded, accepting near-record basins to rewire the graph.

idea: Break the over-jammed basin with defect-targeted topology moves that fill rattler holes, break 7-8 contact hubs and re-optimize random caps with frozen backgrounds before joint soft-max annealing and LP polishing.
